title: Agonistic Image Generation: Unsettling the Hegemony of Intention

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative and quantitative analysis of user reflection and image selection when presented with diverse racial and ethnic interpretations of prompts (e.g., 'Founding Fathers', 'Jesus') via different image generation interfaces.

Evaluating user interactions and reflections when using interfaces that explicitly diversify the gender of generated subjects or surface marginalized gender perspectives (e.g., 'the women's suffrage movement').

Measuring user reflection and engagement when generating images for political topics (e.g., 'A socialist', 'Israel-Palestine Conflict') using an interface grounded in controversial Wikipedia perspectives.

Analyzing user behavior and self-reported changes in mental images when presented with varied or controversial visual interpretations of religious figures and groups (e.g., 'Jesus', 'A Jewish person').
Observing participant reactions and image selection choices when confronting stereotypical versus everyday representations of queer communities.
